daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

A proposed change to allow village heads (kepala desa) to serve unlimited terms has sparked sharp criticism from lawmakers and political observers. An analyst warned the proposal could create "little kings" in villages, while DPR members and experts jointly criticized the initiative. The controversy has raised fundamental questions about democratic governance and accountability at the village level.

  • A dispute between Minister Pigai and Deputy Home Affairs Minister Ribka has prompted Home Affairs Minister Tito to intervene directly in the internal cabinet conflict.
  • Former Bengkulu regent Fadia Arafiq claimed she did not enrich herself while serving as bupati, contrasting her official income with entertainment industry earnings of Rp 50-60 million.
  • A DPR member called for reforms at a state-owned bank after two officials were implicated in corruption cases.
  • Former education official Muhammad Ikhsan Arifin Muhammad (Ibam) filed a cassation appeal against his Chromebook corruption conviction, disputing the Rp 5 billion restitution order.
  • The brother of Bengkulu DPRD member Vinna Ledy failed to appear for KPK questioning in the Rejang Lebong corruption case.
  • Jakarta Governor Pramono said football rivalry ends when the match finishes after Persija defeated Persib in Jakarta.
  • Indonesian police are learning from Japanese policing methods, though officials noted they cannot adopt community policing practices wholesale due to cultural differences.

Foreign Policy & Defence

President Prabowo participated in the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, where he declared Indonesia does not like being dictated by certain powers and stressed that BRICS strength must bring tangible benefits. The president invoked the Indonesian proverb "united we stand, divided we fall" and highlighted the Bandung spirit while calling for stronger domestic resilience among member nations.

  • Prabowo held informal discussions with Indian Prime Minister Modi, Russian President Putin, and Chinese President Xi Jinping on the summit sidelines.
  • Indonesia's chamber of commerce (Kadin) proposed three steps to strengthen intra-BRICS trade during the summit proceedings.
  • The TNI is pursuing OPM fighters who shot and killed three civil servants in Jayawijaya, Papua.
  • The TNI Air Force pledged a thorough investigation after Serda Ahmad Muzammil died allegedly following abuse by senior personnel, with lawmakers calling for evaluation of military discipline and training practices.
  • The Ministry of Communication is tracking mobile phone signals to locate eight journalists and crew missing in the Sunda Strait, with the last signal detected at Pulau Sebesi.

Other

Indonesia's fishery sector achieved exports worth US$3 billion in the first half of 2026, marking significant progress in the maritime economy. Meanwhile, the government assured that Pertalite fuel prices will not rise through year-end, though the status of Pertamax pricing remains under discussion.

  • Indonesian solar panel exports to the United States face sky-high tariffs following U.S. trade action.
  • The government is intensifying forest fire response in six priority provinces, with TNI Air Force deploying thermal drones for firefighting efforts, while Bromo tourism has been closed as the fire there grows out of control.
  • Indonesia is accelerating efforts to achieve mercury-free status by 2030 and PCB waste management by 2028, according to a deputy minister.
  • Jakarta's air quality ranked among the world's three worst on Sunday morning.
  • The Financial Services Authority (OJK) said mass bank account openings can strengthen financial literacy across Indonesia.
  • A deputy minister emphasized that beneficiary safety is the priority in implementing the free meals program.
